# `/parley:parley`

This skill covers:

- [What you produce](#what-you-produce): the document, the review page and the answers file.
- [The loop](#the-loop): check, serve, listen, hand over the link, reply, new round or render.
- [Blocks](#blocks): find a block type step by step. `writing.md` has sources and questions.
- [Revising](writing.md#revising): what to change between rounds.
- [Reference](#reference): the files beside this one, and when to read each.

## What you produce

You write a document, `docs/parley/<id>.json`. Parley turns it into a review page. The reviewer
reads it, comments on any item, answers your questions and gives a verdict. Their words land in
`docs/parley/<id>.answers.json`, and you reply into it.

Use parley when a person must review something with you and their answers change what you do
next: a design, a schema, a migration, a diff, a plan. A document with no questions is an
explanatory document: the reviewer reads it and finishes.

A document is any mix of blocks, in any order, down to one `prose` block.
`node parley.mjs new <id>` writes the smallest valid one to `docs/parley/<id>.json`.

Other skills write parley documents for their own subjects, such as craft's `explain` and
`discuss`.

`parley.mjs` sits in this skill's folder. Run it from the project root, as
`node <this folder>/parley.mjs <command>`; the commands below write it `node parley.mjs`. `bun` and
`deno run -A` work the same as `node`. `node parley.mjs <command> --help` lists a command's flags.
`node parley.mjs` alone lists the commands by group, and `node parley.mjs help` lists the help
topics; `node parley.mjs help <topic>` teaches one. Every command takes `--json`. Each result ends
with `next:` lines that name the likely next commands.

## The loop

Read `loop.md` before the first step. Each step links its rules there.

1. [Check](loop.md#check): `node parley.mjs check <doc.json>`; fix what it prints, warnings too.
2. [Serve](loop.md#serve): `node parley.mjs serve [dir]` in the background, left running. The page
   opens any tracked file; share a `--host 0.0.0.0` token link only with repo readers.
3. [Listen](loop.md#listen): `node parley.mjs answers <id> [dir] --wait` as a background command.
   Don't poll, and don't hand the wait to a subagent.
4. [Hand over the link](loop.md#hand-over-the-link): `node parley.mjs open <id>`, only once a
   listener runs.
5. [Reply to each send](loop.md#reply-to-each-send): `--reply <thread id>`, then listen again.
   Every send stays pending until you reply.
6. [New round or render](loop.md#new-round-or-render): on `[verdict]`, revise
   ([writing.md](writing.md#revising)) or render. When the review is over,
   [stop](loop.md#status-and-stop) the server.

## Blocks

Each block has an `id`, a `type` and an optional `title`. Every item inside has an `id` too. Ids
are unique across the document. Do not read the whole field reference; find the block you need in
steps:

1. `node parley.mjs blocks` lists the categories.
2. `node parley.mjs blocks <category>` lists the types in one.
3. `node parley.mjs blocks search <text>` or `blocks search tag:<name>` finds types by what they
   show.
4. `node parley.mjs block <type>` prints the purpose, the fields and a minimal example. Add
   `--field <path>` for one field in full, `--example` for the whole example to copy, or `--schema`
   for the JSON Schema. The path is a top-level field or dotted into list items, such as
   `node parley.mjs block diff --field findings.severity`.

`writing.md` has the rules for sources, questions and revising.

## Editing

Edit a document by item id; do not rewrite the JSON. Every edit is checked and written only if the
result passes `check`.

- `node parley.mjs new <id> [dir]` starts a document.
- `get <doc> [item]` reads the outline, or one item with what is around it. `--field <path>`
  prints one field.
- `set <doc> <item> <path>=<text>` sets fields. `<path>:=<json>` sets a JSON value.
- `add <doc> [--in <item>] [--after <item>] <path>=<value>...` adds a block, a question or an item.
  `--from <file>` takes the entry as JSON.
- `remove <doc> <item>` and `move <doc> <item> --after|--before|--in <item>`.
- `apply <doc> ops.json` applies a list of ops as one edit, for changes that pass `check` only
  together, such as a step's text and its anchor.

`remove` and `add` refuse an item or id that has comments or answers; `--force` overrides it, so
read the thread first. `add` and `move` also take `--before <item>`.

`<doc>` is a path or an id in `docs/parley`. `node parley.mjs help ids` explains item ids.

## Reference

These files sit beside this one. Each line says when to read it.

- `loop.md`: the rules for each loop step. Read it before the first step.
- `writing.md`: sources, questions and revising. Read it before you write a question or revise.
- `answers.md`: what the page shows, what reaches you and when, and the answers file. Read it
  when a send or the answers file is unclear.
- `glossary.md`: the one name for each parley idea. Read it before you name one in prose.
- `examples/`: whole documents that pass `check`, in folders by subject. Start from the closest.
- `reference-notes.json`: the field notes that `parley block` and `parley schema` print. Do not read
  it; the commands do. Keep it beside `parley.mjs`.
- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES`: the licenses of the packages bundled into `parley.mjs`. Do not read it.
  Keep it beside `parley.mjs`.
